history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Hu-Bu-Lan-Kar Monastery is a small historic Buddhist gompa in the centre of Kalpa village, Kinnaur district, set among traditional wooden houses with the Kinnaur Kailash range behind it. It is said to have been founded by the great translator Rinchen Zangpo (Rinchensang-po, 950/958-1055 CE), who translated Sanskrit Buddhist texts into Tibetan and founded a chain of monasteries across Kinnaur and Ladakh; reviews note it functioned as a monastery-cum-centre of learning for locals. The monastery porch has a white chorten at the centre, rows of prayer wheels all around, and fine wooden carvings on the doors and structure. TRADITION FLAG: it is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery - the specific school (Gelug vs Kagyu vs other) is NOT established by any consulted source (verify before labelling). town_description: Kalpa (historically Chini) is a hillside village in Kinnaur district, Himachal Pradesh, at about 2,759-2,960 m on the old Hindustan-Tibet road above Reckong Peo. Local Kinnauris follow a syncretism of Hinduism and Buddhism, and the village is known for apple orchards, traditional wooden houses, views of the Kinner Kailash shivling rock, the Narayan Nagini Hindu temple, and this old Buddhist gompa.
tradition: Buddhism (Tibetan Buddhist monastery; specific school - Gelug/Kagyu/other - NOT verifiable from consulted sources, flagged for verification)
